Fraunhofer FDK AAC Codec Library
================================

Eclipsa Studio's audio engine contains the AAC decoder of the Fraunhofer
FDK AAC Codec Library, linked in through iamf-tools, which uses it to
decode AAC-LC substreams of IAMF files. Eclipsa Studio never encodes AAC:
its export codecs are LPCM and Opus.

  Project:    Fraunhofer FDK AAC Codec Library for Android
              https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/aac
  Version:    commit ee76460efbdb147e26d804c798949c23f174460b, unmodified
              (the pin in iamf-tools' MODULE.bazel at the commit
              engine/MODULE.bazel names)

              angewandten Forschung e.V.

              for Android (the full text follows)

The complete source code of the FDK AAC Codec as built into Eclipsa
Studio is the repository above at that commit; Eclipsa Studio carries no
modifications to it. The library is statically linked into the audio
engine (libeclipsa_studio_engine.dylib on macOS,
eclipsa_studio_engine.dll on Windows).

---- NOTICE ----

FFmpeg + dav1d
==============

Eclipsa Studio's FFmpeg-in-engine video backend (the "FFmpeg" option in
Settings -> Video backend) decodes the reference video with FFmpeg, plus
dav1d for AV1 (engine/video/, issue ES-249). Both are linked DYNAMICALLY and
shipped as separate shared libraries alongside the audio engine — on macOS in
"Eclipsa Studio.app/Contents/Frameworks" (libav*.dylib), on Windows beside
eclipsa_studio_engine.dll (avcodec-*.dll and the other av*/dav1d DLLs); no
part of FFmpeg or dav1d is statically linked into Eclipsa Studio.

FFmpeg
------
  Project:    FFmpeg — https://ffmpeg.org  (https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg)
  Version:    release n8.0
  Copyright:  © the FFmpeg developers
  License:    GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or later
              (LGPL-2.1-or-later)

  The bundled build is configured WITHOUT --enable-gpl and WITHOUT
  --enable-nonfree, so it contains only LGPL-licensed code. It is a
  decode-only build (encoders, muxers, avdevice, avfilter, postproc and
  networking disabled) with autodetection off, carrying no external
  dependency other than dav1d (below) and system frameworks. Shipped
  libraries: libavutil, libavcodec, libavformat, libswscale, libswresample.

dav1d
-----
  Project:    dav1d — https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d
  Version:    release 1.5.1
  Copyright:  © VideoLAN and dav1d authors
  License:    BSD 2-Clause (see LICENSE.dav1d.txt)

  Linked into libavcodec as the AV1 decoder and shipped as libdav1d.dylib.

Modifying / replacing the bundled libraries (LGPL v2.1 section 6)
----------------------------------------------------------------
In accordance with section 6 of the LGPL v2.1, you may modify the bundled
FFmpeg libraries and use modified versions with Eclipsa Studio: replace the
shipped FFmpeg shared libraries with your own build of interface-compatible
libraries and the application will load them — the libav*.dylib files in
"Eclipsa Studio.app/Contents/Frameworks" on macOS, or the av*-*.dll files
beside eclipsa_studio_engine.dll on Windows. The corresponding source for the
bundled build is FFmpeg at the release listed above
(https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg) and dav1d at its release
(https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d); the exact build configuration is
recorded in engine/deps/ffmpeg/build_ffmpeg.sh (macOS) and
engine/deps/ffmpeg/build_ffmpeg.ps1 (Windows).
